## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 Parallels also occur in Chinese and Sanskrit Dharmapada/Udānavarga traditions (T 210.22, T 212.28, T 213.27, UV 27, and Tibetan Uv Kg 27), and the text is cited in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (*Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*, Ne 37).

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus reflects extensive Pali-internal text reuse, sharing 20 passages with the commentary (*Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*), 4 matches with *Upacālātherīgāthā* (§4.1–0.2), 3 with the *Bhikkhunī Saṁyutta* (SN 5), 2 with the *Sīsūpacālātherīgāthā* (Thig 8.1), 2 with the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37), and 2 with the *Cāpātherīgāthā* (Thig 13.3) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments by DharmaNexus align the text with the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99, fascicle 45) and the *Bieyi Za ahan jing* (T 100, fascicle 12) [DharmaNexus]. Comparative Āgama scholarship similarly records Chinese Saṁyuktāgama discourse parallels concerning Māra's confrontation with the nun Cālā (折羅比丘尼) [Bingenheimer 2011].
